AAAs are usually treated with surgical repair in ruptured, symptomatic or appropriately sized aneurysms. When indicated, unruptured aneurysms can undergo elective repair Newer minimally invasive techniques extend aortic aneurysm treatment into an increasingly elderly population. Recommend elective repair for the patient at low or acceptable surgical risk with a fusiform AAA that is ≥5.5 cm in males and >5cm in females.

blocks.text: If an AAA ruptures, emergency surgical repair is required. The primary repair methods are as follows:
Open - This requires direct access to the aorta via a transperitoneal or retroperitoneal approach

Endovascular - This involves gaining access to the lumen of the abdominal aorta, usually via the femoral vessels; an endograft, typically a polyester or Gore-Tex graft with a stent exoskeleton, is placed within the lumen of the AAA, extending distally into the iliac arteries

blocks.text: Intermittent claudication is one of the most common manifestations of peripheral arterial occlusive disease (PAOD) caused by atherosclerosis. It is characterized by reproducible ischemic muscle pain that occurs during physical activity and is relieved by a short period of rest. The pain results from inadequate blood flow to the affected limb.

Varicose veins and telangiectasia (spider veins) are dilated, elongated and tortuous superficial veins of lower limbs, the visible surface manifestations of an underlying problem with reverse venous flow, which is also termed venous insufficiency syndrome. Mild forms of venous insufficiency are merely uncomfortable, annoying, or cosmetically disfiguring, but severe venous disease can produce serious systemic consequences and can lead to loss of life or limb.

blocks.text: The goals of lymphedema management are to restore limb function, reduce swelling and associated physical and psychological morbidity, prevent recurrent infections and other complications, identify and treat the underlying cause in secondary lymphedema, and promote weight management and regular physical activity to improve clinical outcomes and reduce disease progression.

blocks.text: Conservative measures for managing lymphedema include the following:
Maintenance of appropriate hygiene and skin care
Use of complex physical therapy (first-line treatment) and compression stockings

Surgical treatment is indicated for selected patients with refractory lymphedema and is intended to reduce limb volume, improve lymphatic drainage, and enhance function and quality of life. Surgery is palliative rather than curative and should be used as an adjunct to, not a replacement for, ongoing conservative management, including compression therapy and skin care.
